From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kasˈka.ta/
  • Rhymes: -ata
  • Hyphenation: ca‧scà‧ta

Etymology 1

[edit]

From cascare +‎ -ata; cognate with Piedmontese cascà; from Latin cāsus (“fallen”).

Noun

[edit]

cascata f (plural cascate)

  1. cascade, waterfall
  2. (informal, rare) fall
  3. cascade (hairpiece for women)
Derived terms
[edit]
  • a cascata
  • lista a cascata
Descendants
[edit]
  • → French: cascade
    • → Danish: kaskade
    • → Dutch: cascade
    • → English: cascade
    • → German: Kaskade
    • Haitian Creole: kaskad
    • Mauritian Creole: kaskad
    • → Romanian: cascadă
    • Seychellois Creole: kaskad
    • → Swedish: kaskad
  • → Maltese: kaskata
  • → Portuguese: cascata
  • → Spanish: cascada
    • → Catalan: cascada
See also
[edit]
  • rapida
  • cataratta

Etymology 2

[edit]

Participle

[edit]

cascata f sg

  1. feminine singular of cascato

Anagrams

[edit]
  • saccata

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
cascata
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian cascata (“cascade, waterfall”), ultimately from Latin cāsus (“fallen”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kasˈka.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kasˈka.tɐ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /kaʃˈka.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /kasˈka.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐʃˈka.tɐ/

  • Rhymes: -atɐ
  • Hyphenation: cas‧ca‧ta

Noun

[edit]

cascata f (plural cascatas)

  1. cascade
    1. waterfall
    2. series of events
    3. big lie
  2. (informal) vagina (woman's genitalia)
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:vagina

Derived terms

[edit]
  • cascatear

  • “cascata”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
